# Watchdog workflow

Test baseline workflow catches regressions during AI-assisted development.

## Session start

Watchdog blocks code edits until approved scope written (below) —
every session starts read-only: define scope first, then implement.
At **beginning of every session**, before any work:

1. Call the `watchdog_init` tool to reset session state
2. Spawn `watchdog-baseline-runner` subagent via subagent tool (plugin-registered, uses the plugin's `model` option, then the `title` agent's model, then OpenCode's default selection — baseline mechanical, no reasoning needed): runs QA (lint, format, types) + tests, saves outputs to `.opencode/session/test-baseline.txt`, returns summary
3. While subagent runs, primary agent does what only it can: analyse task, draft scope proposal (Scope definition below) — parallel, session still read-only
4. Relay baseline summary to user: QA pass/fail, total tests, pass/fail counts, coverage percentage
5. QA or tests already failing → flag to user; failing baseline needs explicit user acknowledgement before work starts
6. Session still read-only here — next: Scope definition; edits unlock once scope agreed and written

No subagent support in environment → run baseline inline (QA, tests, save to `test-baseline.txt`), then scope.

## Scope definition

Watchdog blocks all code edits until `.opencode/session/scope.txt`
lists at least one real path, then restricts edits to those paths.
Writing agreed scope **is** the approval — no separate agent or tool.
Before any implementation:

1. Finalise draft scope from session start (analyse task, identify files and directories to modify, where not already done)
2. Present plan and proposed scope to user, **agree it** with them
3. User approves in chat (e.g. "approved", "go") → write approved paths to `.opencode/session/scope.txt`, one path or directory prefix per line (writes into `.opencode/session/` always allowed). Listed paths unblocked from then.

**Ordering:** write `scope.txt` in **own** tool call before any code
edit. Scope checked before each command runs — same-shot write
(`... > scope.txt && ... > file`) fails check. Keep scope write
separate.

Write `scope.txt` only after user approval; edit block stands until
then. Task evolves beyond scope → agree expanded scope with user,
update `.opencode/session/scope.txt`.

## Fast path (trivial changes)

One-line fix, typo, comment, doc/string tweak, version bump → skip
baseline/latest ceremony (session-start QA + tests, summary, session-end
drift compare). Fast path only when change cannot plausibly affect
behaviour or tests. Anything larger (logic changes, multi-file edits,
new functionality) → full workflow above.

Scope enforcement always applies: edits still need
`.opencode/session/scope.txt` entry. Commit gate still applies
(`git commit` needs `test-baseline.txt` and `test-latest.txt` to
exist) — on fast path write one-line note into each file (e.g.
"fast path: trivial change, baseline skipped") to satisfy it without
full run.

## Session end

Before finalising session (user says done, asks for commit, or wrap-up):

1. Spawn `watchdog-baseline-runner` subagent via subagent tool, target file `.opencode/session/test-latest.txt`: runs QA + tests, saves both outputs, returns summary (no subagent support → run inline)
2. Compare against `.opencode/session/test-baseline.txt`
3. Report drift:
   - New QA failures (lint, format, types)
   - New test failures
   - Reduced coverage
   - Tests removed or skipped
4. QA or tests regressed → commits and PRs need explicit user approval first

> **Note**: Plugin blocks `git commit` if `test-baseline.txt` or `test-latest.txt` missing. Plugin = enforcement layer; instructions = behavioural layer. `watchdog_health` tool reports session health anytime.
<!-- watchdog-end -->

# @relf108/opencode-watchdog

Guardrails plugin for [opencode](https://opencode.ai): catches hallucination
and context drift during agent sessions, enforces an agreed edit scope, and
gates commits behind a test baseline.

## What it does

- **Scope enforcement** — all edits (`edit`/`write`/`patch`, plus
  statically-analysed shell writes) are blocked until
  `.opencode/session/scope.txt` lists at least one approved path, then
  restricted to those paths. Writing the agreed scope IS the approval.
- **Commit gate** — `git commit` is blocked until `test-baseline.txt` and
  `test-latest.txt` exist in the session dir.
- **Drift tracking** — consecutive tool errors (warn at 3, block at 5),
  duplicate searches, edit volume, and same-file edit loops.
- **Danger-gate** — a three-tier safety net for auto-mode, covering shell
  commands, reads of secret paths (SSH keys, cloud credentials, keychains —
  hard-blocked), and outbound `webfetch` URLs:
  1. deterministic deny-list (keychain/SSH/credential access, `curl | sh`,
     `rm -rf`, force-push, …) → hard block, no model;
  2. obviously-safe allow-list → pass through, no latency;
  3. everything else → the **`watchdog-auditor`** subagent judges intent
     alignment against the recent conversation (SAFE/RISKY, fail-open on
     error).
- **Custom tools** — `watchdog_init` (reset session state) and
  `watchdog_health` (session health report).
- **Workflow instructions** — bundled `instructions.md` is injected into the
  model's instructions automatically.

## Install

Requires OpenCode V2 with the `@opencode/plugin` 2.1.1 API or newer compatible
2.x release. This version no longer exposes the V1 plugin function.

For OpenCode V1, pin `@relf108/opencode-watchdog@1.0.1`. See
[release notes](CHANGELOG.md) for the V2 migration changes.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@relf108/opencode-watchdog"]
}
```

With options:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "@relf108/opencode-watchdog", "options": {
      "sessionDir": ".opencode/session",
      "dangerGateLLM": true,
      "instructions": true,
      "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
    }}
  ]
}
```

Env fallbacks: `WATCHDOG_SESSION_DIR`, `WATCHDOG_DANGER_GATE_LLM`.

## Bundled agents

The plugin registers two ordinary opencode subagents. Both use the plugin's
`model` option if set, else the `title` agent's model (the V2 replacement for
`small_model`), then OpenCode's default selection. Define your own agent of the
same name in `opencode.json` or an agent file to override any of it — the plugin
only registers a bundled definition when no user definition exists.

- **`watchdog-auditor`** — the LLM tier of the danger-gate. Deny-all
  permissions (a gate must never execute what it judges) and a visible
  intent-alignment prompt.
- **`watchdog-baseline-runner`** — mechanical QA/test executor spawned via
  the subagent tool at session start (writes `test-baseline.txt`) and session end
  (writes `test-latest.txt`) while the primary agent keeps working. Read-and-
  run only: no webfetch, no external directories, no `watchdog_*` tools.

The auditor uses V2 transient session generation, which cannot invoke tools.
Its temporary child session is removed after each verdict. Guardrails accept
V2 `shell`/`patch` tools and the older `bash`/`apply_patch` names.

## CLI

The engine is also runnable from a shell (useful for humans; the plugin
itself calls it in-process):

```
node cli.mjs init | check-scope | check-commit | track-error | track-edit | track-search | health
```

Requires a checkout (or installing `@relf108/opencode-watchdog` as a regular npm
dependency, which exposes the `watchdog` bin). Installing it as an opencode
plugin does **not** put the bin on your path — opencode keeps plugins in its
own cache, not your project's `node_modules`.

## Session state

Lives in `<sessionDir>` (default `.opencode/session`) — gitignore it:

```
scope.txt            approved edit scope, one path/prefix per line
test-baseline.txt    QA + test results at session start
test-latest.txt      QA + test results at session end
errors.count / edits.log / searches.log
```

# Changelog

## 2.0.1

- Move `@opencode/plugin` to development dependencies. The runtime uses no SDK
  imports, so installing watchdog no longer downloads the SDK's dependency tree.

## 2.0.0

### Breaking changes

- Require OpenCode V2 with the `@opencode/plugin` 2.1.1 API or a compatible
  newer 2.x release. OpenCode V1 users must stay on watchdog 1.0.1.
- Replace the V1 plugin function with a V2 plugin definition and default export.
- Use `plugins` configuration with `{ "package": "...", "options": {} }` entries.
- Replace the `small_model` fallback with the `title` agent's model, then
  OpenCode's default model selection.

### Changes

- Register agents, tools, workflow instructions, and execution hooks through
  the V2 plugin API.
- Support V2 `shell`, `patch`, and `path` tool inputs while retaining the older
  `bash`, `apply_patch`, and file-path argument aliases.
- Run danger-gate classification through transient, tool-free generation and
  remove temporary auditor sessions after each verdict.
- Keep concurrent classification deduplication scoped to the calling session.
- Use tool-event agent identity for baseline-runner exemptions.
- Track failed shell executions and count only successful edits.
- Store session state in the loaded checkout rather than the canonical checkout.
